cohort: 144 pregnant women with b-thalassemia minor and 142 women without b-thalassemia, all with singleton pregnancies over 20 weeks of gestation without complications, referred to hospitals affiliated with Shiraz University of Medical Sciences.
finding: Pregnant women with b-thalassemia minor had a significantly higher frequency of low birth weight and placental abnormalities (gross abnormalities, chorangiosis, calcification, syncytial knot, and umbilical cord position) compared to women without b-thalassemia.
